scenarios.title: Pass settings to a child report
scenarios.summary: Repair variable values and export choices while preserving settings supplied by the caller.
scenarios.objective: Repair the setup for a supplied child report. Set SITE from the first supplied argument ($1) and MODE from the second supplied argument ($2), preserving each value exactly, including empty values, spaces and literal wildcard text. Export those two settings; preserve TEAM and every other supplied environment setting with its original value and export attribute. Pass no additional names to the child. The setup must print nothing, finish successfully (exit status 0), and leave all simulated files unchanged. The supplied read-only child must receive the required settings and produce its expected report for every input set.

guide.title: Inspect supplied and created values
guide.why: A supplied environment setting may already be exported; a newly created variable is not.
guide.action: Read the supplied arguments and environment values beside the Setup editor before changing the script. Keep the read-only child report in view.

guide.title: Repair the setting that crosses the boundary
guide.why: The grade checks actual values and export attributes, then runs the child with that resulting environment.
guide.action: Use the Introduction and separate Try example to investigate assignment versus export. Repair the assignment draft without printing a replacement report.

guide.title: Check every input set
guide.why: Spaces, literal wildcards and empty values reveal assumptions that a single successful report can hide.
guide.action: Select Run setup + child. Inspect the first failing case's Parent values and Child output, then edit and retry. Stop cancels unfinished work without awarding completion.

scenarios.explanation: Export controls which current values are copied to a subsequently started child. The required report comes from that child's real simulated environment, while the parent keeps the requested working values and the virtual files stay unchanged.
hints: Which assignment overwrites a supplied value instead of creating one from an argument? Remove the overwrite; do not hard-code a replacement team.
Compare SITE and MODE in Parent values. A value can exist there while its export attribute is off.
Pass the two created settings onward without exporting scratch variables. Existing supplied settings should keep their values and attributes.
scenarios.simplifications: Sources checked 2026-11-04: GNU Bash manual and current LPIC-1 v5.0, objective 103.1 (narrow defining/referencing/exporting slice). In-process evaluator17 runs a bounded parent setup and a separate immutable supplied child; no operating-system process is created. Supported here: global ordinary scalar assignments, literal export NAME / NAME=value, Bash export -n NAME, and documented simple commands/if decisions. C/POSIX behavior is fixed; LANG, LANGUAGE and LC_* environment controls are refused. No startup files, PATH search, temporary command environments, function/pipeline/loop/array/substitution scopes or xtrace in environment activities. At most 128 observed names and 16 KiB of values; each setup is at most 8 KiB, with shared execution/memory/output bounds. This is not complete 103.1 or 105.1 coverage.
scenarios.retry_guidance: First distinguish a script error from a state mismatch. Compare the named variable's parent value and export attribute with the missing or unexpected child setting; do not print a look-alike child report from the setup. Then run every sample again.

teaching.prerequisite_note: First complete basic file navigation and shell arguments. You should recognize a script, comments, quoted values and printf. This lesson introduces child environments and export; no Linux setup or real command launch is needed.

concepts.title: Values in this script and values passed onward
concepts.text: A shell variable gives a name to a value. The environment is the set of named values passed to a newly started program. Here, your setup is the parent script and the supplied report is the child. Creating a variable in the parent does not automatically pass it to the child.

concepts.title: Supplied values are different from names you create
concepts.text: The example supplies HOST and two arguments. $1 means the first argument; $2 means the second argument. LOCATION="$1" creates LOCATION from the first argument, with no spaces around =. HOST already arrived in the environment, so it is already marked for export: keep its supplied value. In the assignment, TEAM is supplied; SITE and MODE are names you create from the arguments.

concepts.title: Select the values the child receives
concepts.text: export LOCATION STYLE marks both names for later child programs. It does not print them or change their values. Assignment and export may be separate, as shown below, or combined as export LOCATION="$1". Quotes make it clear that spaces and literal * characters belong to one value.

concepts.title: Read a missing setting without confusing it with empty text
concepts.text: The assignment child also prints a Region line. In its read-only script, ${REGION-<not supplied>} uses REGION when it is set and prints <not supplied> when the name is absent. An existing empty REGION stays a blank field. You do not need to write this syntax; use it to understand that report.

concepts.title: Run the setup, then inspect the child
concepts.text: Run example first evaluates the setup, then runs a separate simulated report using the exported values. The read-only child uses printf: %s inserts one text value and backslash-n (\n) ends the line. The setup stays quiet. The child receives a copy of the selected values. A finished program returns a number called its exit status; 0 means it completed successfully. A successful assignment or export already returns 0, so you do not need to add an exit command.

teaching.example:
# HOST is supplied; leave its value unchanged.
LOCATION="$1"
STYLE="$2"
export LOCATION STYLE
teaching.inputs: Gallery preview supplies HOST=visitors and arguments Gallery North / short. Workshop preview supplies HOST=makers and Tea Room / large print. The setup has no output; each child prints Host, Location and Style on three lines.
teaching.try_change: Remove LOCATION from the export line, then Run example. Compare Parent value, Child receives and Child report · actual. Restore LOCATION and run again.

STYLE="$2"
export LOCATION STYLE
export -n REMINDER

solution:
SITE="$1"
MODE="$2"
export SITE MODE
export -n NOTE
scenarios.explanation: Export controls which current values are copied to a subsequently started child. The required report comes from that child's real simulated environment, while the parent keeps the requested working values and the virtual files stay unchanged.
hints: An empty assignment changes NOTE's value but does not remove its export attribute. Preserve the supplied note, including when it is already empty.
Compare NOTE and TEAM in Parent values. They have different child-visibility requirements; unexporting the wrong name breaks the inherited team.
Bash export -n removes an export attribute without deleting the parent value. The supplied child checks whether NOTE is absent, not whether it prints as empty.
scenarios.simplifications: Sources checked 2026-11-04: GNU Bash manual and current LPIC-1 v5.0, objective 103.1 (narrow defining/referencing/exporting slice). In-process evaluator17 runs a bounded parent setup and a separate immutable supplied child; no operating-system process is created. Supported here: global ordinary scalar assignments, literal export NAME / NAME=value, Bash export -n NAME, and documented simple commands/if decisions. C/POSIX behavior is fixed; LANG, LANGUAGE and LC_* environment controls are refused. No startup files, PATH search, temporary command environments, function/pipeline/loop/array/substitution scopes or xtrace in environment activities. At most 128 observed names and 16 KiB of values; each setup is at most 8 KiB, with shared execution/memory/output bounds. This is not complete 103.1 or 105.1 coverage.
scenarios.retry_guidance: First distinguish a script error from a state mismatch. Compare the named variable's parent value and export attribute with the missing or unexpected child setting; do not print a look-alike child report from the setup. Then run every sample again.

teaching.prerequisite_note: Complete Pass settings to a child report first. This lesson reuses assignments, arguments, quoting and export, then adds Bash export -n and the difference between an empty value and an unset name.

concepts.title: Keep a value here without passing it on
concepts.text: This lesson separates a parent working value from child-visible settings. REMINDER is supplied to the example and initially exported. Bash export -n REMINDER removes that export attribute while keeping the exact parent value. An assignment such as REMINDER='' changes the value instead; it does not remove the export attribute.

concepts.title: Empty and absent mean different things
concepts.text: An empty value exists but contains no text. An unset name has no value. In the read-only report, ${REMINDER-<not passed>} substitutes <not passed> only when REMINDER is unset. Without a colon after the name, an existing empty value stays empty. After unexporting REMINDER, the parent still has its supplied value, but the new child has no REMINDER.

concepts.title: Preserve the other inherited settings
concepts.text: HOST still belongs in the child environment. Removing REMINDER's attribute must not remove HOST's or overwrite a supplied value. LOCATION and STYLE are created from the two arguments and exported, just as in the previous lesson. Each input set starts with its own sample values and reset simulated files.

concepts.title: Bash-specific control, bounded practice
concepts.text: export NAME and ordinary assignments are portable shell concepts. The -n option is Bash-specific. It affects subsequently started children; it does not rewrite a child that is already running or change your own desktop environment.
